concept.name: Liquidation threshold
concept.definition: The liquidation threshold is the per-asset percentage of collateral value at which a borrow position is deemed undercollateralized and becomes eligible for liquidation — effectively the maintenance margin of a DeFi loan.
concept.intuition: It is the tripwire on your collateral: once your debt exceeds this share of what you posted, the protocol declares the loan unsafe and lets liquidators step in.
concept.mechanics: Aave Governance sets a liquidation threshold per asset (e.g. 80% for ETH, 97-98% for stablecoin E-Mode). The account's weighted average threshold enters the health factor formula; when HF falls below 1, a liquidationCall repays up to 50% of debt (100% if deeply insolvent) and seizes collateral at a discount. The threshold sits above LTV, giving borrowers a buffer between max borrow and liquidation.
concept.formula: Position liquidatable when: borrows > Σ(collateral_i × liquidation threshold_i).
concept.failure_modes: Thresholds set too high for volatile assets let insolvency arrive before liquidators can profitably act; governance misconfiguration or oracle errors can liquidate healthy users or fail to liquidate dying ones.
concept.misconceptions: The liquidation threshold is not the same as max LTV — LTV limits new borrowing, the (higher) threshold triggers liquidation; confusing them leads borrowers to think max-borrowed positions are safe. It is a parameter, not a market-derived guarantee.
concept.example: With ETH's 80% threshold, a borrower with $10,000 ETH and $7,900 debt is still safe (HF ≈ 1.013), but a further $150 drop in collateral value or $150 of accrued interest crosses HF < 1 and opens the position to liquidators.

citations.source: Frangella & Herskind, Aave V3 Technical Paper (2022)
citations.section: Section 3-4: risk parameters (LTV, liquidation threshold, liquidation bonus)
